origin.description: Bind vectors, matrices, and arrays along one margin. This is a generalization of cbind and rbind.
origin.usage: abind(..., along=N, rev.along=NULL, new.names=NULL, force.array=TRUE, make.names=use.anon.names, use.anon.names=FALSE, use.first.dimnames=FALSE, hier.names=FALSE, use.dnns=FALSE)

arguments.text: Vectors, matrices, arrays, or data frames. Every dimension must agree except the one named by along. One list is accepted in place of several arguments.

arguments.name: along
arguments.text: The margin to bind on. The default is the last dimension. A fraction, a number below 1, or a number past the current rank inserts a new dimension.

arguments.name: rev.along
arguments.text: Sets along to N + 1 - rev.along and ignores a supplied along. rev.along = 0 adds a dimension after the last.

arguments.name: new.names
arguments.text: A list supplies dimnames. A character vector supplies argument names, and empty strings are ignored.

arguments.name: force.array
arguments.text: When false and the result is two-dimensional, the call is passed to cbind or rbind.

arguments.name: hier.names
arguments.text: before, after, or none. TRUE is before. FALSE leaves the margin names unchanged.

arguments.name: use.first.dimnames
arguments.text: Take dimnames from the first argument that has them. The default keeps the last, as cbind and rbind do.

arguments.name: use.dnns
arguments.text: Keep names of the dimnames. use.first.dimnames chooses which source wins.

origin.details: A vector is treated as one dimension. An argument with one fewer dimension gains a size-1 margin at along. Dimension names on the bound margin come from existing names, otherwise from the argument name.
origin.value: An array. The length of its dim is the common rank, or one more when along creates a dimension.

translation.description: Bind vectors, matrices, and arrays along one margin. This is a generalization of cbind and rbind.
translation.usage: abind(*arrays, along=None, rev_along=None, new_names=None, force_array=True, make_names=None, use_anon_names=False, use_first_dimnames=False, hier_names=False, use_dnns=False, **named)

arguments.name: *arrays
arguments.text: Vectors, matrices, arrays, or data frames. Every dimension must agree except the one named by along. One list or dict of arrays is the single list argument.

arguments.name: along
arguments.text: The margin to bind on. The default is the last dimension. A fraction, a number below 1, or a number past the current rank inserts a new dimension.

arguments.name: rev_along
arguments.text: Sets along to N + 1 - rev_along and ignores a supplied along. rev_along = 0 adds a dimension after the last.

arguments.name: new_names
arguments.text: A nested list supplies dimnames. A list of strings supplies argument names, and empty strings are ignored.

arguments.name: force_array
arguments.text: When false and the result is two-dimensional, the call follows cbind or rbind.

arguments.name: hier_names
arguments.text: before, after, or none. True is before. False leaves the margin names unchanged.

arguments.name: use_first_dimnames
arguments.text: Take dimnames from the first argument that has them. The default keeps the last, as cbind and rbind do.

arguments.name: use_dnns
arguments.text: Keep names of the dimnames. use_first_dimnames chooses which source wins.

translation.details: A vector is treated as one dimension. An argument with one fewer dimension gains a size-1 margin at along. Dimension names on the bound margin come from existing names, otherwise from the argument name. Keyword arguments other than the formals are those names.
translation.value: An array. The length of its dim is the common rank, or one more when along creates a dimension.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from abind.abind import abind
print(abind(x=np.arange(1, 5), y=np.arange(5, 9)))
